acceptance_criteria.criterion: Navigating to #/repositories renders a table listing all repositories with ID, Name, and URL columns fetched from GET /api/repositories.
The 'Add Repository' form validates that URL is provided (required), accepts optional Name and ID fields, calls POST /api/repositories on submit, shows a success toast, and refreshes the table.
Inline edit functionality allows changing a repository's Name and persists the change via PUT /api/repositories/:id.
Clicking Delete shows a confirmation dialog warning that the repo will be removed from all projects; confirming calls DELETE /api/repositories/:id and removes the row.
API errors during any CRUD operation are displayed as error toasts via showToast().

summary: Full CRUD Repositories view implemented in gui/public/js/views/repositories.js and wired into app.js. All 40 QA tests pass (0 failures).

No issues found in touched files — code is clean and consistent.

comments.note: No blocking issues — code is clean, consistent with established view patterns (dashboard.js, project-detail.js), and well-commented throughout. Function decomposition (buildTableHead, buildRepoRow, renderRepoTable, buildAddRepoSection, renderRepositories) is excellent: each function has a single clear responsibility and is appropriately scoped.

normaliseRepo() in repositories.js correctly handles Go-style capitalised keys (Id, Name, Url), lowercase keys, and the URL alias (repo.URL) — matches the identical function in project-detail.js. The key ordering (Url before URL) is intentional and consistent.

saveBtn state management (disabled + textContent mutation in finally block) is correct and prevents double-submit. Same pattern used correctly in the Add form's submitBtn and in deleteBtn. Consistent across all three async action handlers.

The showConfirm() rejection-as-cancel pattern (try/catch with empty catch body) is the established project idiom — intentional and correct. The comment '// User cancelled — do nothing.' makes intent explicit.

[documentation-forward] normaliseRepo() is defined identically in both repositories.js and project-detail.js. This duplication is low-risk now (two files) but will compound as more views are added. The README or an architecture doc should note that a shared js/utils/normalise.js (or similar) is the intended future home for these per-entity normalisation helpers, so the next developer knows where to put similar functions and when to extract the shared module.
